title: Satisfiability by simplification and branching
summary: Simplify clauses under partial assignments, justify unit and pure-literal rules, and prove a terminating search returns a model exactly when one exists.
abstract: Suppose several requirements say which switches must be on or off, and which combinations are allowed. Rather than try every complete setting immediately, we can record a few choices and simplify what remains. A requirement with only one alternative forces the next choice; a switch that occurs in only one direction can be set safely. When neither observation settles the problem, we try its two settings in turn. We prove precisely what these simplifications preserve and give a finite search that either constructs a satisfying setting or correctly reports that none exists.

based_on.title: Logic and Mechanized Reasoning (Release 0.1)
based_on.pages: §§6.2–6.3 (partial assignments, unit propagation, pure literals, and DPLL)
